extracted.intended_audience: legislators, copyright offices, lawyers, rights-holders (authors, performers, producers), libraries and cultural institutions in Member States of the Organization
extracted.subtask_description: A regional treaty-style annex setting definitions, scope, protected subject-matter, rights (moral and economic), exceptions, terms of protection, ownership, assignment and special contract rules for copyright and related rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "reproduction"
rubrics_metrics.description: "reproduction" means the making of one or more copies of a work or of a part of such work in any form whatsoever that enable it to be communicated to the public by indirect means; it may be effected inter alia by printing, drawing, engraving, photography, molding, all graphical and plastic art processes, mechanical, cinematographic or magnetic recording; for architectural works, reproduction also consists of repeated execution of a master plan or model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists many means (printing, drawing, photography, molding, mechanical, cinematographic, magnetic recording). Explicitly includes repeated execution for architectural works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "reprographic reproduction"
rubrics_metrics.description: "reprographic reproduction" means the making of facsimile copies of originals or copies of a work by means other than painting, in particular by any photographic or similar process, including in databases or photocopying, printing, digitization and storage information systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies photographic/similar processes, digitization and storage systems as reprographic reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "copy"
rubrics_metrics.description: "copy" means the outcome of any act of reproduction of a work already fixed on a medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "computer program"
rubrics_metrics.description: "computer program" means a set of instructions expressed in words, codes, schemes or any other form capable, once incorporated in a machine-readable medium, of performing a task or obtaining a particular result by means of a computer or by an electronic process capable of processing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers various forms of expression (words, codes, schemes) and machine-readable incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "database"
rubrics_metrics.description: "database" means a compilation of data or of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "public lending" and "rental"
rubrics_metrics.description: "public lending" means the transfer of possession of the original or of a copy of a work for a limited period for non-profit by an institution providing services to the public; "rental" means transfer of possession of the original or a copy for a limited period for profit-making purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes purpose (non-profit lending vs profit-making rental).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "distribution"
rubrics_metrics.description: "distribution" is the offering for sale or rent or any other act of putting into circulation, for valuable consideration, of the original or copies of a literary or artistic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "entertainment promoter"
rubrics_metrics.description: "entertainment promoter" is any natural or legal person who occasionally or on an ongoing basis performs protected works or causes them to be performed in an establishment that admits the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "accessible format copy"
rubrics_metrics.description: "accessible format copy" means a copy of a work in an alternative manner or form which gives a person with visual impairment access to the work, including to permit access as feasibly and comfortably as a person without visual impairment or other print disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines aim of accessible format: comparable access for visually impaired persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "authorized entity"
rubrics_metrics.description: "authorized entity" means an entity authorized or recognized by the government of a Member State to provide education, instructional training, adaptive reading or information access to persons who are blind, visually impaired or otherwise print disabled on a non-profit basis; includes government institutions or non-profits providing such services as primary activity or institutional obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: "visually impaired"
rubrics_metrics.description: "visually impaired" means a person who is blind or has a visual impairment, a perceptual or reading disability which cannot be improved to give visual function substantially equivalent to a person without such impairment, or is otherwise unable, through physical disability, to hold/manipulate a book or to focus/move the eyes normally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers blindness, uncorrectable impairment, and physical inability to manipulate reading materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: territorial and nationality criteria for protection
rubrics_metrics.description: This Annex applies to works whose author or other original copyright holder is a national of a Member State or has habitual residence/headquarters in such State; works published for the first time on the territory of a Member State or published first abroad and also published in a Member State within 30 days; and works of architecture erected in one of the Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of joint authorship, it suffices that one joint author meets the nationality/residence requirement. Cross-references to the Agreement Revising the Bangui Agreement and other international treaties remain unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection begins at creation
rubrics_metrics.description: The author of any original work of the mind shall enjoy, by the mere fact of its creation, an exclusive incorporeal property right enforceable against all persons; protection begins with creation and the work is taken to be created independently of any fixing on a material medium or disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work includes creations made with the aid of an automatic process and is protected even if incomplete, by mere personal embodiment of the author's conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected subject-matter: works covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Annex applies to literary and artistic works constituting original creations of the mind in literary, artistic and scientific fields, including: works expressed in writing (including computer programs); lectures, addresses, sermons; musical works; dramatic works; choreographic works and mimed works; audiovisual works; fine art (drawings, paintings, sculptures, engravings, lithographs); works of architecture; photographic works; works of applied art; illustrations, maps, plans, sketches and 3D works relating to geography, topography, architecture or science; and traditional cultural expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection is independent of mode/form of expression, quality, and purpose of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative works and collections are protected
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations, adaptations, arrangements and other transformations of works and expressions of folklore, and collections of works or simple facts/data (encyclopedias, anthologies, databases) are protected where by reason of selection, coordination or arrangement they constitute creations of the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection of derivative works does not affect protection of pre-existing works used in their making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter not protected
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection shall not extend to: official texts of a legislative, administrative or judicial nature or their official translations; news of the day; and simple facts and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral rights (core)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independently of economic rights and even after assignment, the author has the right to: (i) claim authorship, have name affixed to copies and, where possible, in relation to public use; (ii) remain anonymous or use a pseudonym; (iii) oppose any distortion, mutilation or other modification or action derogatory to the work prejudicial to his honor or reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral rights are vested in the person of the author, perpetual, inalienable, not subject to time limitations, indefeasible, and transferable after death to heirs; exercise may be transferred testamentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to disclose and conditions on reconsideration/withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: An author has the exclusive right to disclose his work and shall determine the disclosure process and conditions. The author has the right to reconsider or withdraw, even after publication, with respect to the assignee, but may exercise it only if he indemnifies the assignee for any prejudice caused; if he later decides to republish, he must offer exploitation rights first to the original assignee under original conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic rights (enumerated acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: An author enjoys exclusive right to exploit his work in any form and to obtain monetary advantage; in particular the exclusive right to: (i) reproduction; (ii) translation, adaptation, arrangement or other transformation; (iii) distribution of copies to the public by sale or other transfer of ownership or by rental or lending; and (iv) public performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to Articles 10–24 (exceptions and limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rental right limitation for computer programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The rental right shall not apply to rental of computer programs where the program itself is not the essential subject matter of the rental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resale royalty (droit de suite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of graphic and three-dimensional works, and of manuscripts, have an inalienable right to participate in the proceeds of any sale of such work or manuscript by public auction or through a dealer; this does not apply to works of architecture or works of applied art; conditions and rates determined by competent national authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free reproduction for private purposes (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permitted to reproduce a lawfully published work exclusively for the private use of the user without consent or remuneration, subject to exceptions in paragraph (2): reproduction of architectural works as buildings; reprographic reproduction of an entire book, works of fine art, graphical presentation of musical works, and certain one-time publications; reproduction of whole or significant parts of databases; reproduction of computer programs except as provided in Article 17; copies of software other than backup copy; and any reproduction that would prejudice normal exploitation or cause unwarranted prejudice to legitimate interests of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private-use reproduction is narrow and excludes many types of works and reproductions that impair normal exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation permitted (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permitted to quote a lawfully published work in another work without consent or remuneration, on condition that source and author are stated (if given) and the quotation is compatible with fair practice and its extent does not exceed that justified by the intended purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free use for teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permitted to use a lawfully published work without consent or remuneration as an illustration in publications, broadcasts or sound/visual recordings intended for teaching, subject to stating the source and name of the author if given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprographic reproduction by libraries and archives
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-profit library or archive may, without consent or remuneration, make individual copies by reprographic reproduction: (i) for preserving/replacing lost/destroyed/unusable copies, or replacing a copy lost/destroyed/unusable in another library's permanent collection; and (ii) for preservation or to preserve conditions for consultation for research or private study by individuals on premises or dedicated terminals of libraries open to the public, museums or archival services, provided no economic/commercial benefits are sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditioned on non-profit status and preservation/consultation purposes; reproduction must not be for economic benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free reproduction for judicial and administrative purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permitted to reproduce a work intended for a judicial or administrative procedure to the extent justified by the intended purpose without consent or remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free use for informatory purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to stating source/name if given, it is permitted without consent/remuneration to: (i) reproduce in press or audiovisual means an economic/political/religious article published in newspapers/periodicals where rights not expressly reserved; (ii) reproduce or make available to the public, for reporting on current events, a work seen or heard during such event to extent justified; (iii) reproduce political speeches, lectures, sermons or pleadings given in public for information and extent justified, unless authors have expressly reserved their rights. Authors retain exclusive right to publish collections of such works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free use of images of works permanently located in public places
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permitted without consent or remuneration to reproduce, broadcast or communicate to the public by cable an image of a work of architecture, fine art, photographic work or applied art that is permanently located in a place open to the public, except if the image is the main subject of such reproduction/broadcast/communication and it is used for profit-making purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits incidental images of public works; main-subject commercial uses are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free use and adaptation of computer programs (lawful user rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: A lawful user of a copy of a computer program may, without consent or separate remuneration, make a copy or an adaptation of the program if: (i) necessary for the use of the program for the purposes for which it was obtained; or (ii) necessary for archiving and to replace a lawfully held copy that has been lost/destroyed/unusable. No copy/adaptation may be made for other purposes and any copy/adaptation shall be destroyed where prolonged possession ceases to be lawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow user-right exceptions limited to legitimate use and archival/backup; not a general right to adapt for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ephemeral recording by broadcasting organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: A broadcasting organization may make an ephemeral recording by its own facilities for purposes of its own broadcasts of a work it is authorized to broadcast, without consent or separate remuneration; the recording shall be destroyed within six months unless a longer period is agreed with the author; in absence of agreement, a single copy may be kept for exclusive record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free performance exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A work may be publicly performed without consent or remuneration in the following circumstances: (i) within a family circle provided no income is generated; (ii) at official ceremonies to the extent justified by the nature of the ceremonies; (iii) at religious ceremonies on premises intended for that purpose; (iv) as part of activities of a teaching establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importing for personal purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A natural person may import a copy of a work for personal purposes without consent of the author or any other holder of the copyright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody, pastiche and caricature
rubrics_metrics.description: A parody, pastiche or caricature of the work may be created without consent or payment, having regard to the laws governing the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free use for the visually impaired
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a literary work is published or made available to the public in any form, the author may not prohibit access by means of reproduction, distribution or making available to a visually impaired person; access is achieved where the visually impaired person, an authorized entity or primary caretaker makes a special format provided they have lawful access to the work or a copy; cross-border supply of accessible format copies to authorized entities or persons in foreign countries is allowed; Member States may establish compensatory remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically allows creation and international non-commercial supply of accessible format copies and contemplates compensatory remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free provisional (transitory) reproduction in networks
rubrics_metrics.description: A transitory or accessory reproduction may be made without authorization where it is an integral and essential part of a technological process with the sole goal of enabling the lawful use of the work or its transmission among third parties through a network requiring an intermediary; such provisional reproduction may only pertain to works other than software and databases and shall not have intrinsic financial value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets transient caching/technical copies needed for network transmission; excludes software/databases and monetary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of distribution rights (first-sale doctrine)
rubrics_metrics.description: On authorization of the first sale of one or more hard copies of a work by the author or his successors in title in the territory of a Member State or another State, the sale of such copies may no longer be prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopts principle that distribution right is exhausted after lawful first sale in territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exceptions: non-impairment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The exceptions set forth may not impair the normal exploitation of the work or be unjustly prejudicial to the legitimate rights of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General three-step-like safeguard limiting exceptions to avoid harm to normal exploitation and legitimate interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection: general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic rights shall be protected during the lifetime of the author and for 50 years after his death; moral rights shall be without limit in time; after expiry of economic rights the national collective rights management body shall be entitled to ensure compliance with moral rights for the benefit of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes lifetime + 50 years for economic rights, perpetual moral rights, and post-expiry role for collective management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection: joint authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic rights in a work of joint authorship shall be protected during the lifetime of the last surviving author and for 50 years after his death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection: anonymous and pseudonymous works
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic rights in an anonymously or pseudonymously published work shall be protected for 50 years from the end of the year in which the work was lawfully published for the first time or, failing such an event within 50 years, from other specified dates tied to making or disclosure; if the author's identity is disclosed prior to expiry, ordinary provisions for identified authors apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex fallback rules ensure at least 50 years of protection from publication/making dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection: collective and audiovisual works
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic rights in a collective work or audiovisual work shall be protected for 50 years from the end of the year in which the work was lawfully published for the first time or, failing that within 50 years from making or making accessible dates as alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection: works of applied art
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic rights in a work of applied art shall be protected for 25 years from the making of such work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits provided shall expire at the end of the calendar year during which they would normally lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All terms are calculated to the end of the calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership: author as first owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The author of a work shall be the first owner of the moral and economic rights in his work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership in works of joint authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint authors are the first joint owners of the copyright; if a joint work can be divided into independent parts, each joint author may exploit the independent part he created while remaining joint owner of the whole, provided such exploitation is not prejudicial to exploitation of the joint work; collaboration should be the subject of a collaboration agreement; joint authors exercise rights by mutual agreement; benefits are due in proportion to contribution unless otherwise agreed; joint authors may terminate a contribution failed to be completed due to refusal or force majeure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages contractual clarity and proportionate sharing; courts have jurisdiction for disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of collective works
rubrics_metrics.description: The first owner of moral and economic rights in a collective work is the natural or legal person on whose initiative and under whose responsibility the work was created and who published it under his name; joint authors of contributions retain right to exploit their contributions independently unless prejudicial to the collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership in works created under a work contract or on commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Entering into a contract to rent a work or a service contract by an author does not entail waiver of copyright unless otherwise stipulated in writing; where a work is created on behalf of a person under such a contract or commissioned, the first owner shall be the author, but economic rights shall be deemed transferred to the employer to the extent justified by the habitual activities of the employer at the time of creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumes author ownership unless written stipulation to the contrary; employer transfer limited to what is justified by habitual activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership in commissioned advertising works
rubrics_metrics.description: For a commissioned work used for advertising, the first owner of economic and moral rights is the author; nonetheless, the contract between producer and author shall, unless otherwise agreed, entail assignment to the producer of rights of exploitation provided the contract states discrete remuneration for each form of exploitation with regard to geographical area, duration, volume of print and nature of medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires explicit contractual remuneration details for assigned exploitation rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership in audiovisual works (assumed joint authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: First owners of moral and economic rights in an audiovisual work shall be the joint authors; unless otherwise proven, joint authors are assumed to include the director, author of screenplay, author of adaptation, author of dialogue, composer of specially created music and the producer; authors of previously existing works adapted or used are regarded as joint authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates presumptions about which contributors are joint authors unless rebutted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of ownership for disclosed authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless proven otherwise, the author is the person under whose name or pseudonym the work is disclosed; for anonymous/pseudonymous works the publisher whose name appears is considered to represent the author unless the author reveals identity and proves entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of rights: economic vs moral
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic rights are assignable by transfer intra vivos and by testament or by effect of law by reason of death; moral rights shall not be assignable intra vivos but may be assigned by testament or by operation of law by reason of death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing: exclusive and non-exclusive licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: An author may grant licenses to carry out acts covered by economic rights; licenses may be non-exclusive (entitling holder to perform authorized acts at same time as author and other non-exclusive licensees) or exclusive (entitling holder to carry out authorized acts to the exclusion of any other person, including the author); no license may be deemed exclusive unless expressly stipulated in the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration of authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The remuneration of the author shall be proportionate to the operating revenue; it may be a flat rate where the basis for calculation cannot be determined by practical means, or the use of the work is ancillary to the exploited object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows flat-rate remuneration in limited, specified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of assignment and license contracts (writing requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: On pain of invalidity, contracts for assignment of economic rights or grant of licenses shall be concluded in writing, including on electronic media in accordance with domestic legislation in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts not in writing are invalid for assignment/licensing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of assignments/licenses (territory, duration, means)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total assignment of future works shall be invalid. Assignments and licenses may be limited to specific rights and with respect to aims, duration, territorial scope and extent or means of exploitation. Failure to mention territorial scope is deemed to limit assignment/license to the country where made; failure to mention extent or means of exploitation is deemed to limit to scope and means necessary for the aims envisaged when making the assignment/granting the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rules favor limiting ambiguous assignments/licenses to avoid unintended broad transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between ownership of the medium and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership of a work is independent of ownership of the physical object; unless otherwise stipulated, the acquirer of the original or a copy is not vested by acquisition with any of the rights provided for in this law (those remain with the author or successors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing, author-expense and joint-expense contracts (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A publishing contract is one under which the author assigns to a publisher the right to make sufficient copies which the publisher is required to publish and disseminate; 'contract at the author's expense' and 'contracts at joint expense' are distinguished as service-like arrangements where author(s) pay publisher to make and disseminate copies and share profits/losses respectively, and do not constitute publishing contracts under paragraph (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates true publishing contracts from author-funded or joint-funding arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of the publisher
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher must furnish author with all evidence required to establish accuracy of accounts; must effect manufacture in conditions/form/mode provided in contract; ensure continuous exploitation and distribution for sale according to professional custom; make no changes to the work without written authorization of the author; and unless otherwise agreed, display the name/pseudonym/mark of the author on each copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher duties include accounting transparency, faithful manufacture, continuous exploitation and respect for author attribution and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation contracts and collective management
rubrics_metrics.description: A representation contract authorizes a legal or natural person to represent the work in conditions determined by the author; a general representation contract is where a collective management organization vests a person with power to represent current or future works of the repertoire for the duration of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses delegation of representation to agents and collective management organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of entertainment promoters
rubrics_metrics.description: An entertainment promoter must inform the author or agents of the exact program of public performances and furnish a certified statement of takings; must effect public performance under technical conditions suitable to ensure the intellectual and moral rights of the author; may not transfer the enjoyment of the contract without the consent of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promoter duties protect authors' moral and economic interests and require transparency of takings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audiovisual production contracts: producer's rights and authors' retention
rubrics_metrics.description: An audiovisual production contract creates a producer who takes initiative/responsibility; contract between producer and joint authors (other than musical authors) shall entail assignment of exclusive rights in the work to the producer unless otherwise provided, while joint authors shall retain their graphical and theatrical rights and right to exploit contributions separately unless otherwise agreed and provided such exploitation is not likely to compete with exploitation of the whole; remuneration as authors is due for each mode of exploitation and paid by the producer; producer must provide statements and proof of accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances producer's commercial control with authors' retained rights and mandates remuneration and accounting transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of joint authors and producer (guarantees and accounting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint authors must guarantee to the producer the peaceful exercise of the assigned rights. The producer must ensure exploitation in accordance with professional custom and provide joint authors with a statement of income from exploitation at least once a year and, on request, provide proof of accuracy of the accounts and copies of relevant contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes mutual obligations: authors must not undermine assigned rights; producer must provide accounting and income transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (performers, fixation, phonogram, phonogram producer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performer: actors, singers, musicians, dancers and other persons who perform literary or artistic works or traditional cultural expressions. Fixation: incorporation of sounds, images or both in a material medium permanent or sufficiently stable to permit perception, reproduction, or communication. Phonogram: any exclusively sound fixation of sounds from a performance or other sounds. Phonogram producer: natural or legal person who is first to take initiative and responsibility for fixing sounds from a performance or other sounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes terms used in rights-related provisions applying to performers and phonogram producers.
